questions.text: Can you tell me what you do?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Lewis, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Can you tell me what you do?

questions.text: Would you recommend your job or subject to a friend? Why?

cueCard.topic: Describe something interesting you saw on social media.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you found it interesting.

questions.text: Describe something interesting you saw on social media.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe something interesting you saw on social media. You should say: what it was; where you saw it; when you saw it; and explain why you found it interesting.

questions.text: Did you share it with anyone?
questions.say: Thank you. Did you share it with anyone?

questions.text: Why do people spend so much time on social media?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about something interesting you saw on social media, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all social media. Why do people spend so much time on social media?

questions.text: What are the dangers of social media for teenagers?
questions.say: What are the dangers of social media for teenagers?

questions.text: Has social media changed the way people make friends?
questions.say: Has social media changed the way people make friends?

questions.text: How can people tell whether information they see online is true?
questions.say: Now let's talk about information online. How can people tell whether information they see online is true?

questions.text: Should social media companies be responsible for false information on their sites?
questions.say: Should social media companies be responsible for false information on their sites?

questions.text: Do people get most of their news from social media nowadays?
